targets.title: Is depression taxonic, dimensional, or both?
targets.evidence_quote: To illustrate the utility of simulated comparison data for evaluating the suitability of data and facilitating the interpretation of results, we conducted taxometric analyses in two samples using the IDS indicators chosen by Beach and Amir (2003).
targets.outcome_quote: In fact, the present results closely mirrored those obtained by Beach and Amir, but parallel analysis of simulated comparison data clearly revealed these results to be more indicative of dimensional than taxonic structure. Further replication within a clinical sample characterized by a high rate of depressive pathology similarly refuted Beach and Amir’s original taxonic interpretation of IDS.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Independent college and clinical samples refute the central original claim of a taxonic structure. Similar raw curves do not confirm that substantive finding. The text explicitly describes the samples as drawn from similar populations, rather than reanalysis of Beach and Amir data.
